subQuestion.question: (1) The minimum distance between the start and finish points of the motion of an object is called the ________.
subQuestion.ans: displacement of the object.

subQuestion.question: (2) ________ is negative acceleration.
subQuestion.ans: Deceleration

subQuestion.question: (3) When an object is in uniform circular motion, its ________ changes at every point.
subQuestion.ans: velocity

subQuestion.question: (4) During collision total ________ remains constant.
subQuestion.ans: momentum

subQuestion.question: (5) The working of a rocket depends on ________.
subQuestion.ans: Newton’s third law of motion

subQuestion.question: (1) The velocity of an object at rest is considered to be uniform.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The velocity of an object at rest is always zero.
(2) Thus, it does not change with time. Hence, it is considered to be uniform.

subQuestion.question: (2) When an object falls freely to the ground, its acceleration is uniform.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) When an object falls freely, the only force acting on the object is that due to the earth’s gravity.
(2) Near the earth’s surface, this force on a given object is practically uniform. Hence, an object falling freely to the ground has almost a uniform acceleration.

subQuestion.question: (3) Even though the magnitudes of action force and reaction force are equal and their directions are opposite, their effects do not get cancelled.
subQuestion.ans: Action and reaction forces act on different bodies. Hence, though their magnitudes are equal and directions are opposite, their effects do not get cancelled.

subQuestion.question: (4) It is easier to stop a tennis ball as compared to a cricket ball, when both are travelling with the same velocity.
subQuestion.ans:
(1) The momentum of a body is the product of its mass and velocity. The mass of a cricket ball is greater than that of a tennis ball. Hence, if the two balls have the same velocity, the momentum of the cricket ball will be greater than that of the tennis ball.
(2) Also a cricket ball is harder than a tennis ball. Therefore, it is easy to stop a tennis ball than a cricket ball moving with the same velocity.

subQuestion.question: Distance
subQuestion.ans:
1. Distance is the length of the actual path followed by a body between the points under consideration.
2. It does not have direction.
3. It is greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.

subQuestion.question: Displacement
subQuestion.ans:
1. Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial point to the final point of movement of a body.
2. It has direction.
3. Its magnitude is less than or equal to the distance.

subQuestion.question: Uniform Motion
subQuestion.ans:
1. A body is said to have uniform motion when it covers equal distances in very small equal intervals of time.
2. In this case, the speed of the body is constant.

subQuestion.question: Nonuniform Motion
subQuestion.ans:
1. A body is said to have nonuniform motion when it covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time.
2. In this case, the speed of the body is not constant.

subQuestion.question: An object of mass 16 kg moving with an acceleration of 3 m/s². Calculate the applied force. If the same force is applied on an object of mass 24 kg, how much will be the acceleration?
subQuestion.ans:
Data: m₁ = 16 kg, a₁ = 3 m/s², F = ?, m₂ = 24 kg, a₂ = ?

(i) F = m₁a₁ = 16 kg × 3 m/s² = 48 N
The force acting on the object = 48 N

(ii) F = m₂a₂
∴ a₂ = F / m₂ = 48 N / 24 kg = 2 m/s²
The acceleration of the object = 2 m/s²

subQuestion.question: An object moves 18 m in the first 3 seconds, 22 m in the next 3 seconds, and 14 m in the last 3 seconds. What is its average speed?
subQuestion.ans:
Data: s₁ = 18 m, t₁ = 3 s, s₂ = 22 m, t₂ = 3 s, s₃ = 14 m, t₃ = 3 s, average speed = ?

Average speed = (total distance travelled) / (total time taken)
= (s₁ + s₂ + s₃) / (t₁ + t₂ + t₃)
= (18 m + 22 m + 14 m) / (3 s + 3 s + 3 s)
= 54 / 9 m/s = 6 m/s
The average speed of the object = 6 m/s

subQuestion.question: A bullet having a mass of 10 g and moving with a speed of 1.5 m/s penetrates a thick wooden plank of mass 90 g. The plank was initially at rest. The bullet gets embedded in the plank and both move together. Determine their velocity.
subQuestion.ans:
Data: m₁ = 10 g = 10 × 10⁻³ kg, u₁ = 1.5 m/s, m₂ = 90 g = 90 × 10⁻³ kg, u₂ = 0 m/s, v₁ = v₂ = v = ?

By the law of conservation of momentum,
m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂
As u₁ = 0 m/s and v₁ = v₂ = v, we have
m₁u₁ = (m₁ + m₂)v
∴ v = (m₁u₁) / (m₁ + m₂)
= (10 × 10⁻³ kg × 1.5 m/s) / (10 × 10⁻³ kg + 90 × 10⁻³ kg)
= (10 × 1.5) / 100 m/s = 0.15 m/s
The speed with which the plank containing the bullet moves = 0.15 m/s
